Injection 3 already attained the maximum CRF with substantial resolution margin. Shorten its gradient by one grid step while keeping temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to seek a faster fully resolved method.

Injection 9 retains maximum CRF with a minimum resolution of 4.53, leaving ample margin for further compression. Shorten the gradient another grid step while holding solvent endpoints and temperature fixed to test a faster fully resolved separation.

The 4-minute gradient still provides a minimum resolution of 3.34 and maximum CRF. Test the shortest permitted gradient with the same solvent endpoints and temperature to reduce elution time while checking whether the early pair remains fully resolved.

The last peak elutes during the final hold, so increase phi1 by one grid step to accelerate it. Keep phi0 and temperature unchanged to limit selectivity changes while testing whether the early pair retains R ≥ 1.5 under the slightly steeper gradient.

Raise phi1 one more grid step to shorten the last peak’s hold-phase retention. The early pair’s resolution decreased only from 1.85 to 1.72 in the previous step, suggesting this change may preserve full resolution and maximum CRF.

Test the highest permitted final organic fraction to further shorten the last peak’s retention. The early pair is approaching the resolution limit, so this single-step change will establish whether the faster method still achieves R ≥ 1.5 throughout.

With gradient duration and final organic fraction already at their limits, test a one-step temperature increase to shorten retention further. The early pair has almost no resolution margin, so this run will determine whether temperature helps selectivity or pushes the method below full resolution.

Lower phi0 one grid step to test whether increased early retention restores the first pair’s resolution at 30 C. Keep the short gradient and strong final solvent to preserve rapid elution of the last compound.

Lowering phi0 worsened the early pair, suggesting the steeper gradient outweighed the benefit of increased initial retention. Return to 25 C and test phi0 one step above the fastest fully resolved method to narrow the gradient window and potentially shorten elution while retaining full resolution.

Increasing phi0 to 0.25 improved the critical pair’s resolution and slightly shortened the last retention time. Test one further step at 25 C to locate the best initial organic fraction before early-peak retention becomes too weak.

The narrower solvent window has increased the early pair’s resolution to 1.77, providing margin for a modest temperature increase. Test 30 C to shorten the separation while checking that this pair remains above R = 1.5.

Test one further temperature step to establish the speed–resolution boundary for the fastest fully resolved method. The early pair may fall below R = 1.5; if it does, retain injection 19 as the faster maximum-CRF option.

At 35 C, only the early pair loses resolution; reduce phi1 to make the gradient shallower and test recovery of R ≥ 1.5 while retaining a short run. Injection 19 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-CRF method.

The early pair barely responded to slope at phi0 = 0.30, consistent with elution near the gradient’s arrival. Lower phi0 one step to retain these peaks further into the gradient and test whether full resolution can be recovered at 35 C.

Reduce phi1 one grid step to spread the early pair, which is now retained beyond the gradient’s arrival but remains just below full resolution. This tests a maximum-CRF alternative at 35 C while injection 19 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.

Injection 23’s early pair is still flagged below threshold despite rounding to 1.50, so return to 30 C to improve selectivity. Use phi1 = 0.90 to accelerate the last peak while retaining a shallower gradient than the marginal phi1 = 0.95 methods.

Test a slightly shallower gradient than injection 19 to seek additional early-pair resolution margin while keeping all peaks well within 10 minutes. Injection 19 remains the fastest demonstrated maximum-CRF method; this final run evaluates a potentially more robust alternative.
